Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Leila (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Raj (ParcelAI ML Eng), Maria (ParcelAI CTO), Nina (ParcelAI Infra), Samir (ParcelAI Product), Olga (QA)

Summary: Console demo of Optimize quantization sweep and tradeoffs. Ran live sensitivity examples, looked at sample prompt failures, discussed rollout and security. Agreed on next steps to exchange eval sets and run a pilot.

--- Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect) ---
Topics covered: quantization sweep, int8/fp8 comparison, latency vs quality graphs, A/B rollout, VPC/private deployment questions, SOC2 and KMS.
Action items (auto-detected): Send spreadsheet, share pilot plan, provide eval prompts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE for ParcelAI. We'll do a quick run through Optimize, focus on quantization profiles — INT8 vs FP8 — and practical tradeoffs. Leila and Priya are here to show the console and the sensitivity sweep.
[00:28] Maria (ParcelAI): Thanks — timing's good. We're primarily worried about latency spikes during peak routing, and then any quality regressions on risk-critical prompts.
[00:35] Leila (Redwood): Totally. We'll show p50/p95/p99 and a fidelity check against your eval set (we used a small sample you shared earlier). Note: that sample was anonymized so names changed — but behavior is representative.
[01:12] Raj (ParcelAI): Quick nit — when you say "sweep" are you doing full retraining or is this a post-training quantization? We want no model retrain in our flow.
[01:25] Priya (Redwood): Good question — it's post-training quantization and runtime kernels that support INT8 and FP8. No retrain required; it's binary-compatible model variants and runtime selection.
[01:38] Nina (ParcelAI): Also add infra constraints — we need VPC peering + KMS integration. How does Private handle key management — customer-managed keys or—you manage?
[01:52] Jordan (Redwood): Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs, we can share the SOC2 pack. There was a recent doc update — I'll send the security appendix after the call.
[02:12] Samir (ParcelAI): Can you show an example where INT8 kills latency but FP8 keeps quality? We have some small prompts where hallucination is very expensive.
[02:26] Leila (Redwood): Yep we'll pull that up. I'm switching to the Optimize console now — bear with me.
[02:52] Speaker 7: [inaudible] — switching screens
[03:10] Leila (Redwood): Okay, on screen is the quantization sweep dashboard. X-axis is profile (FP32, FP16 baseline, FP8 variant A, INT8 variant B), Y-axis left is average latency, right is a delta quality score (lower means more error).
[03:33] Raj (ParcelAI): That delta quality metric — is that automatic or did you compute it from our sample human eval?
[03:42] Leila (Redwood): It's computed from your sample eval plus a synthetic scoring function — so it's a mix. We flag any deltas above a threshold and surface examples.
[03:55] [05:00] Leila (Redwood): Look here — FP8 variant shows 1.6x token throughput improvement vs FP32 and only a small 3% drop in our org-level QA score; INT8 shows 2.8x throughput but a wider spread: most prompts are fine but certain edge-case prompts drop to a 12–18% lower score.
[05:27] Raj (ParcelAI): Hmm, those edge cases — are they long context prompts or specific token patterns?
[05:36] Priya (Redwood): In our sweep the failing prompts tend to have lots of numeric tables and nested bullet lists — the quantization errors affect attention precision there. It's fairly consistent with other customers who use highly structured inputs.
[05:50] Maria (ParcelAI): Important to know. For us the routing decisions use compact JSON payloads with tables occasionally. We can't afford critical misroutes.
[06:05] Leila (Redwood): Totally. That's why rollout decisions often pick FP8 for baseline cost/latency, and then INT8 behind a canary that excludes your flagged classes.
[06:20] [07:00] Jordan (Redwood): Quick interjection — on cost guidance: INT8 typically reduces token compute billing by roughly 35–50% versus FP16 on our Dedicated nodes; FP8 is usually a 20–30% reduction with better fidelity. Those are approximate and workload-dependent. We'll provide a more precise per-token projection from your evals.
[07:25] Nina (ParcelAI): Are those cost numbers for hosted or dedicated? Also, if we go private, how does pricing change?
[07:36] Jordan (Redwood): Hosted pricing is simpler; Dedicated is commit-based and can be much cheaper at scale. Private (on-prem) is licensed + infra; costs depend on your hardware, but our Optimize recommendations include quantization to reduce GPU requirements. We'll include a modeled billing sheet for both hosted and dedicated.
[08:02] Raj (ParcelAI): Could we see a live example of a prompt that broke under INT8?
[08:10] Leila (Redwood): Yep — pulling the "examples" tab that shows failing and passing prompts. Here's a failing case (example redacted).
[08:30] [08:45] Leila (Redwood): The transcript shows the model returned a hallucinated URL and mis-ordered list items. In FP8 it returned the right order and no hallucination. INT8 introduced token-level noise around dates.
[09:02] Raj (ParcelAI): OK. Are you using any post-filtering or reranking that could catch hallucinations?
[09:12] Priya (Redwood): We showed a reranking demo in another call — you can combine a lightweight reranker (embedding-based) to catch hallucinations; that adds a little latency but can be configured only for high-risk endpoints.
[09:30] Samir (ParcelAI): So a hybrid — use INT8 for low-risk endpoints, FP8 for moderate, FP16 for high-risk. That maps OK to our product tiers.
[09:45] Leila (Redwood): Exactly. And the Console's policy routing can do that automatically — route by path or token cost or header.
[10:12] [11:00] Maria (ParcelAI): Tail latency — can you speak to p99 under burst? Our SLO is 200ms p95 and 500ms p99 on the routing path.
[11:14] Leila (Redwood): Tail latency depends strongly on KV cache hit rate and batching behavior. INT8 reduces compute but doesn't magically eliminate long-tail queuing. We showed earlier an example where INT8 reduced average latency but p99 still spiked due to cache miss storm.
[11:36] Raj (ParcelAI): Do you have mitigation knobs? Like pre-warming or request shaping?
[11:43] Priya (Redwood): Yes — autoscale, burst capacity, and a smart prefetch for KV cache. Also you can set a soft-fallback to go to an FP8/FP16 replica when latency crosses thresholds. The console has automatic fallback policies.
[12:10] [13:00] Leila (Redwood): I'm switching to the rollout tab — here's an example canary policy: 5% traffic to INT8 for 48 hours, check quality metrics and error rate, if pass — ramp to 25% then 100. You can also do sample-based human checks in the middle.
[13:30] Nina (ParcelAI): For Private deployment, how is telemetry shipped? We need to keep logs within our VPC and not send user content to Redwood.
[13:44] Jordan (Redwood): Private supports a control plane with customer-managed telemetry endpoints; raw inputs can be suppressed. We'll share the privacy matrix.
[13:58] [15:00] Maria (ParcelAI): SOC2 and data residency — we need SOC2 type II and EU data residency for some customers. Is that supported?
[15:10] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — Redwood has SOC2 and we have EU regions. For Private on-prem deployments residency is, of course, in your control. I'll attach the compliance summary.
[15:30] Raj (ParcelAI): Back to sensitivity: can you run an on-the-fly sweep with our supplied 50 prompts? We prepared a small set to replicate the issue.
[15:43] Leila (Redwood): We can run a quick simulated sweep but full results will take longer. I'll run an initial pass now — sanity check.
[16:00] [16:30] Leila (Redwood): Running... okay the job started — showing live progress: we've got latency histogram and per-example delta. A few of your prompts already flagged under INT8.
[16:55] Raj (ParcelAI): Which prompts? The ones with numbers?
[17:05] Leila (Redwood): Yes, mostly table-style prompts and those with repeated date arithmetic. FP8 handles them much better.
[17:20] Samir (ParcelAI): Any idea what % of traffic those represent in production?
[17:28] Raj (ParcelAI): Roughly 8-12% but they cluster in certain flows used by our enterprise customers.
[17:40] Priya (Redwood): In cases like that we'd recommend an exclusion rule in the routing layer: if request header contains X-structured:true or path /enterprise-table, route to FP8. That way you still gain INT8 savings for the other ~90% traffic.
[18:05] [19:00] Maria (ParcelAI): How do we validate quality during rollout — automated metrics only or human review too?
[19:12] Leila (Redwood): Both. Console supports metric-based gates (delta QA, token-level divergence) and a human sampling integration for QA teams. We can forward sampled responses to a secure S3 or VPC endpoint for your QA review.
[19:38] Nina (ParcelAI): On the network side, will we need special egress rules? We already restrict outbound to a tight list of endpoints.
[19:50] Jordan (Redwood): We'll provide the IP ranges and endpoints for telemetry and control plane. For Private we can avoid external egress entirely.
[20:18] [21:00] Leila (Redwood): Going back to benchmarks — here's a table: FP16 baseline, FP8 variant, INT8 variant. Note the p95 latency numbers: FP16 120ms, FP8 95ms, INT8 88ms average; but p99: FP16 300ms, FP8 280ms, INT8 520ms for the specific traffic mix with cache misses. So you get better average but worse tail in some scenarios.
[21:45] Raj (ParcelAI): That p99 jump on INT8 is concerning — what's the root cause?
[21:55] Priya (Redwood): It's a queuing effect amplified by cache miss storms; INT8 uses different kernel that can be single-threaded in corner cases with our current runtime on some GPU families. We're working on a mitigation that parallelizes those kernels — ETA is a few weeks.
[22:20] Maria (ParcelAI): Can we get an SLA credit if we adopt INT8 and it causes regression?
[22:30] Jordan (Redwood): SLA on Dedicated and Enterprise tiers includes uptime and latency targets. Specific performance credits can be negotiated in the commitment contract. We'll flag this as a contractual item to discuss with your procurement.
[22:50] [24:00] Samir (ParcelAI): Any examples of customers who've done a mixed rollout like this — success stories?
[24:08] Leila (Redwood): Yes — a logistics customer used FP8 for customer-facing chat and INT8 for batch scoring with a retrier flow. They saved 40% on inference cost while keeping high-risk flows on FP16/FP8.
[24:30] Raj (ParcelAI): Are we looking at any model quality regressions that affect billing or compliance?
[24:40] Priya (Redwood): Not for most customers; regressions are workload specific. That's why a pilot with your eval set is essential.
[25:05] [26:00] Leila (Redwood): I'm creating a draft rollout policy in the console and saving it as a template — I'll attach the JSON policy to the follow-up email.
[26:20] Maria (ParcelAI): Good. Also want to confirm we can do canary by user-segment rather than by percent.
[26:30] Leila (Redwood): Yep — console supports header-based routing and user-id segmentation.
[26:50] [28:00] Nina (ParcelAI): Security: KMS key rotation and audit logs — will those be visible to our security team?
[28:10] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — logs are configurable. For Private, logs stay in your environment. For hosted accounts we can ship logs to your SIEM via secure channel.
[28:40] Raj (ParcelAI): Anything in the console about automatic rollback triggers? We want a hard stop if quality delta exceeds X.
[28:50] Priya (Redwood): You can set hard gates: if QA delta > 5% or hallucination rate > 1% we automatically rollback.
[29:10] [30:00] Leila (Redwood): Quick note — the sample sweep completed. Summary: Of your 50 prompts, 4 flagged as risky on INT8, 0 flagged on FP8. Quality delta median 2% for FP8, mean 9% for INT8 with outliers.
[30:30] Raj (ParcelAI): Ok that's helpful — do you keep raw logs so we can audit?
[30:38] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — audit logs retained per your retention policy; we can set retention and redaction.
[31:00] [32:00] Maria (ParcelAI): Timeframe — if we agree to a pilot, how quickly can you spin up a dedicated pilot?
[32:12] Jordan (Redwood): We can launch a minimal dedicated pilot within ~7 business days after contract signatures and infra checks. Private on-prem takes longer — typically 4-6 weeks.
[32:30] Nina (ParcelAI): We'll need to loop in procurement on licensing and also connect infra for peering.
[32:42] Jordan (Redwood): Understood. We'll include procurement language and a draft SOW in the follow-up.
[33:00] [34:00] Samir (ParcelAI): Onboarding — who is primary SE from Redwood during the pilot?
[34:08] Jordan (Redwood): Leila and Priya will be primary; I'll be point for commercial and logistics.
[34:30] Raj (ParcelAI): One last technical: what's the expected regression risk if we do int8 with a small KV cache? We are constrained on cache memory.
[34:44] Priya (Redwood): Small KV cache increases attention recompute and can exacerbate INT8 noise on long contexts. For those flows we recommend FP8 or sticky cache for user sessions.
[35:15] [36:00] Leila (Redwood): OK wrapping into the console demo — I exported the sweep results and attached the failing examples. You can see the flagged tokens and the raw model outputs.
[36:30] Raj (ParcelAI): Appreciate that. The raw outputs will help our QA team.
[36:42] Maria (ParcelAI): Are there any vendor lock-in risks with your optimized kernels? If we ever wanted to run in-house — how portable are the quantized artifacts?
[36:55] Jordan (Redwood): Quantized model artifacts are standard formats but some optimized kernels are Redwood-specific for perf. We provide a portability guide — you can run artifacts elsewhere but you may lose the same perf profile.
[37:20] [38:00] Leila (Redwood): Also a note on metrics — we recommend a combination: automated QA delta, embedding similarity to canonical answers, and human pass/fail sampling during canary.
[38:28] Nina (ParcelAI): For the pilot, can we limit the data sent back for telemetry? We need to ensure PII never leaves environment.
[38:40] Jordan (Redwood): Absolutely — we support sampling, redaction, and full suppression. We'll work through the telemetry contract.
[39:02] [40:00] Priya (Redwood): I'm going to outline a recommended pilot plan in the follow-up: 1) baseline run on FP16, 2) FP8 for 2 days, 3) INT8 canary at 5% with hard gates, 4) evaluate and expand. We'll include the exact metrics to watch.
[40:28] Raj (ParcelAI): That sounds reasonable. Can you put expected cost delta for each step?
[40:36] Jordan (Redwood): Yes — Jordan: I'll attach a cost model with expected token savings and projected monthly savings given your traffic volumes.
[41:00] [42:00] Samir (ParcelAI): Any outstanding blockers you need from us to start the pilot?
[42:08] Leila (Redwood): The eval set, a list of endpoints and their traffic proportions, and infra contact for peering are the main ones.
[42:20] Raj (ParcelAI): We'll get that over.
[42:35] [44:00] Maria (ParcelAI): Let's talk procurement — our budget cycle closes end of November, and we want committed savings in Q1. If the pilot shows 30% savings, we'd expedite.
[44:12] Jordan (Redwood): Good to know — we'll prioritize the pilot timeline. We'll include an example commitment schedule.
[44:40] [46:00] Leila (Redwood): Final screen: saved the policy template and the sweep export. I'll share both plus the raw logs we just generated.
[46:15] Raj (ParcelAI): Great. A couple micro-questions — do you have a recommended retry policy for INT8 fallback?
[46:25] Priya (Redwood): Yes — a fast soft-fallback: if p95 > threshold then route to FP8 but keep request counts; a hard fallback calls FP8 replica directly. We'll share sample configs.
[46:50] Nina (ParcelAI): We'll want that config as code (Terraform or CloudFormation).
[47:00] Jordan (Redwood): We have Terraform modules for routing and policy; will include them in the repo link.
[47:22] [48:00] Maria (ParcelAI): Any compliance caveats about storing audit logs in third-party buckets?
[48:10] Jordan (Redwood): For hosted, we recommend shipping to your managed buckets with encryption; Private keeps logs local. We'll add recommended retention and encryption notes.
[48:40] Olga (ParcelAI QA): Regarding flagged prompts — do you recommend synthetic augmentation to reduce sensitivity to INT8?
[48:52] Leila (Redwood): Sometimes data augmentation or prompt re-writing reduces edge-case failures; we can help create a small rewriter to normalize tables.
[49:10] Raj (ParcelAI): That's interesting — could save us from routing complexity.
[49:20] Priya (Redwood): We can prototype a rewriter during the pilot.
[49:45] [50:00] Jordan (Redwood): We're at ~50 minutes — quick recap and next steps. 1) Jordan to share security appendix and cost model by Friday (10/24). 2) Leila to send policy template and sweep export. 3) ParcelAI to send 1k eval prompts and infra contact. 4) Schedule pilot kickoff week of 10/27.
[50:45] Maria (ParcelAI): Sounds good. Anything else?
[50:52] Samir (ParcelAI): No, that's all from Product.
[51:02] Raj (ParcelAI): Thanks — looking forward to the logs.
[51:10] Nina (ParcelAI): We'll start internal approvals.
[51:20] Jordan (Redwood): Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the email and attachments.
[51:35] [57:12] Meeting ended

Notes on transcription fidelity: Speaker labels are mostly accurate but there may be a few mis-attributions and small transcription errors (e.g., kv-cach).
